advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use collections.deque for the BFS worklist in expand_with_disposition_replacements instead of list.pop(0).
evidence: Contrast src/rebar/_snapshot/ticket_view.py:285 `frontier = deque([canonical])` for the analogous descendant BFS
advisory.finding: `expand_with_disposition_replacements` uses `queue.pop(0)` on a list as a FIFO queue, which is O(n) per dequeue (O(n^2) overall) rather than using `collections.deque`; the sibling BFS in ticket_view.transitive_descendant_ids uses a deque.
scenarios: Large evidence scopes with many disposition replacements/descendants.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where the named replacement is archived/deleted, asserting the parent close still fails the landed-work precheck.
evidence: close_scope.py:95 `if state.get("archived") or state.get("status") in {"archived", "deleted"}: return None`
Module docstring line 21 `only a ticket already closed with a close class and naming a live replacement can add that replacement`
ABSENCE: no test in test_close_gate_subtree.py archives/deletes a replacement to confirm its commit is NOT credited
advisory.finding: The live-replacement narrowing is untested: _live_pinned_ticket (close_scope.py:82-97) and replacement_target_for_closed_disposition are documented to credit only a LIVE (non-archived/non-deleted) replacement, but no test exercises the negative path where the named replacement is archived/deleted and therefore must NOT be credited. This named violating input (a duplicate child pointing at an archived replacement that carries a commit) is a newly introduced guard on added lines.
scenarios: Duplicate child names a replacement that was later archived/deleted; the parent must still fail closed because the live-replacement evidence is gone
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that closes the duplicate child naming a replacement, then archives/deletes the replacement (which carries the commit), and asserts `rebar.RebarError` on the epic close.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for a two-hop disposition chain (child->R1->R2) where only R2 carries the referencing commit, asserting the parent closes certified.
evidence: close_scope.py:140-141 `expanded.add(replacement)` then `queue.append(replacement)` — replacements are re-processed for their own dispositions
ABSENCE: all replacement tests are single-hop; none chains R1 -> R2
advisory.finding: Chained/transitive disposition expansion is untested: the queue loop re-enqueues each new replacement (close_scope.py:141) so that a replacement itself closed as a disposition naming a FURTHER replacement is followed transitively. No test exercises a two-hop chain (child duplicates R1; R1 closed duplicate naming R2 which carries the commit).
scenarios: A duplicate child names R1, and R1 was itself closed as a duplicate of R2 which holds the landed commit

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `assert rebar.verify_signature(epic, ...)['verdict'] == 'certified'` to the superseded replacement test to match the duplicate test.
evidence: test_close_gate_subtree.py:168-169 `_close(epic, rebar_repo)` then `assert _status(epic, rebar_repo) == "closed"` with no verify_signature assertion
Duplicate twin at test_close_gate_subtree.py:140 `assert rebar.verify_signature(epic, repo_root=str(rebar_repo))["verdict"] == "certified"`
advisory.finding: test_parent_close_credits_superseded_child_replacement_commit asserts only that the epic status is 'closed' but omits the certified-verdict assertion its duplicate twin makes, so it does not confirm the superseded replacement close is signed/certified rather than merely status-closed.
scenarios: Superseded replacement crediting closes the epic but fails to produce a certified signature
advisory.suggested_fix: Append the verify_signature certified assertion at the end of test_parent_close_credits_superseded_child_replacement_commit.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where the landed commit references a descendant of the replacement ticket (not the replacement itself), asserting the parent closes certified.
evidence: close_scope.py:100-114 `_replacement_descendant_ids(...)` returns transitive descendants of the replacement
Test at test_close_gate_subtree.py:126 `_commit_ref(rebar_repo, replacement)` — commit is on the replacement itself, never a grandchild under it
ABSENCE: no test creates a child under `replacement` and puts the only referencing commit on that grandchild, so the descendant-crediting branch is never exercised
blocking.finding: The replacement-subtree credit path is untested: _replacement_descendant_ids and the queue expansion (close_scope.py:100-114, 142-146) add the replacement's transitive descendants to the evidence scope, but no test places the landed referencing commit on a DESCENDANT of the replacement ticket. Every replacement test (test_parent_close_credits_duplicate_child_replacement_commit, test_parent_close_credits_superseded_child_replacement_commit) commits the trailer directly on `replacement`. If _replacement_descendant_ids returned [] (or the loop dropped descendants), all present tests would still pass, so a regression in this specific added behavior is undetectable.
scenarios: An epic whose duplicate child names a replacement STORY, where the landed commit references a TASK under that replacement story
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a test that creates a child under `replacement`, commits a `rebar-ticket:` trailer referencing only that grandchild, closes the replacement, and asserts the epic closes certified.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Either compute `descendant_ids` before disposition-replacement expansion or rename/emit a distinct metric for the replacement-credited scope.
evidence: close_precheck.py:137 non-pinned path also expands before `metrics["descendant_ids"] = len(accepted_ids) - 1` at 139

The metric is consumed by scripts/rebar_duration_probe.py:159 and asserted in tests/unit/test_close_duration_instrumentation.py (e.g. `"descendant_ids": 0/2`), so a probe reader will attribute replacement-scope tickets to the descendant count.
dropped.finding: The `descendant_ids` metric is computed as `len(accepted_ids) - 1` AFTER `expand_with_disposition_replacements` folds disposition replacement tickets and their entire descendant subtrees into `accepted_ids`, so the metric no longer counts only descendants of the closing ticket — it silently conflates true descendants with credited replacement scope, mislabeling the emitted monitoring field.
scenarios: A parent close where a duplicate child names an out-of-subtree replacement: descendant_ids is inflated by the replacement and its subtree.
